title: Schedule of Lapse Term Loadings on the Credit Reissue Fee — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
The credit reissue fee carried against a fare brand in the Air Ticket Fare Brands tariff is taken at a loading that follows how long the credit has stood unclaimed, and what that loading bears on is the tariff component. The count is made in whole calendar months. The standard-lapse term is 3 months and the long-lapse term is 12 months.

| Time the credit has stood unclaimed | How the tariff component is taken |
| --- | --- |
| Longer than 12 whole calendar months | The tariff component is taken at the long-lapse loading of 1.6 |
| Longer than 3 whole calendar months but not longer than 12 | The tariff component is taken at the standard-lapse loading of 1.25 |
| Not longer than 3 whole calendar months | The tariff component is taken as it stands |

Each term is passed only when the count runs beyond it, and the month at the term itself does not pass it. A credit that has stood unclaimed for 3 whole calendar months has not stood unclaimed for longer than the standard-lapse term, and the tariff component is taken as it stands; at 4 whole calendar months the tariff component is taken at the loading of 1.25. A credit that has stood unclaimed for 12 whole calendar months has not stood unclaimed for longer than the long-lapse term, so the tariff component is still taken at the loading of 1.25; at 13 whole calendar months it is taken at the loading of 1.6.
